newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Petron awards Aug mogas tender, seeks Sept cargo.
newsitem.headline: Petron awards Aug mogas tender, seeks Sept cargo.

text.p: Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp has awarded a tender to buy up to 100,000-barrels of 95-octane gasoline for August 10-20 and is seeking another cargo for early Septmber delivery, traders said on Monday.

South Korean refiner Ssangyong Oil Refining Co was awarded the August tender which closed last week, at less than $5 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, on a cost-and-freight Bataan basis, traders said.
The tender for the early September delivery cargo closes August 4 and is valid until late August 5, they said.
Two weeks ago, Petron cancelled its first gasoline import tender in about two years, because of "operational considerations", a company official said.

Since the cancellation, European major British Petroleum has sold around 100,000 barrels of August delivery 97-octane unleaded gasoline to Petron, through negotiations, at around 60-80 cents per barrel over Singapore 97-octane quotes.

Petron, which operates a 155,000-bpd refinery in Bataan, north of the capital Manila, had not issued a gasoline import tender since 1995 but had to re-emerge to buy due to increased domestic demand, an official had said.
Industry sources also said the August import requirement was also partly due to the unexpected shutdown of a 15,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) thermal cracker on June 20 following an explosion.
The unit, which produces diesel, gasoline and liquefied petroleum gas, is expected to restart mid-August.
The September requirement is due to a shortfall while Petron shuts down for maintenance, a 85,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) No.2 and 17,000-bpd reformer September 1-12, traders said.
